events.text: {sac_name} tells you on a cold night, with the lamps out, so you cannot see {sac_his} face: for nine years {sac_he} has stood at the same gate and it has not opened. {sac_His} hair is going grey at the temples. "I am not afraid of dying," {sac_he} says. "I am afraid of dying here, at this exact step, after all of it."

effects.log: {sac_name} holds on hard. Neither of you lights the lamp. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)
"There is no way," says {sac_name}. "I have looked for nine years." You do not believe that. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)

events.text: {sac_name}, your sworn sibling of the road, has been drinking alone at the inn where you swore the oath. "Remember what we said?" {sac_he} asks. "Same day, same hour, if we die. I have been thinking that I am going to make you a liar. I have been at my wall too long."

effects.log: You drink to the oath again. "Not yet," you say. "Nobody is making anybody a liar yet." (The Wall, in the Jianghu)
{sac_name} tells you: the seclusions, the failures, the sound the meridians make when the gate holds. You listen to all of it. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)

events.text: {sac_name} has always been the strong one, the one who carried you as a child. Now {sac_he} sits on the veranda of the old family house and admits it: the next realm will not come, and the years left are fewer every spring. "Do not tell anyone," {sac_he} says. "I would rather be remembered at the wall than pitied for it."

effects.log: You keep the promise. You also start thinking. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)

choices.text: "You carried me. Let me carry you."

effects.log: {sac_name} laughs, and then does not. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)

events.text: {sac_name} has stood at the same wall for years, and has finally said it aloud to you over tea: the gate is not going to open, and the years are running out. {sac_He} says it plainly, the way one says it will rain. Then {sac_he} asks about your day, as if nothing has been said.

effects.log: You tell {sac_him} about your day. Inside, you are already counting what you have that could be given. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)
"No," you say. "We are talking about this." {sac_name} looks relieved that someone has said it. (The Wall, in the Jianghu)

events.text: {sac_name} goes into seclusion again and comes out after a month, thinner, with blood in the corner of {sac_his} mouth where the qi turned back on itself. "Close," {sac_he} says. "It is always close."

effects.log: The medicine helps the body. Nothing helps the gate.
You sit. {sac_name} sleeps for the first time in a month.

events.text: A younger cultivator, half {sac_name}'s age, passes {sac_his} realm at a sect gathering and bows to {sac_him} with great respect. {sac_name} bows back perfectly, and afterwards breaks a teacup in {sac_his} hand without noticing.

choices.text: Take the pieces out of {sac_his} palm

effects.log: You pick out the pieces one by one. {sac_name} watches you do it and says nothing.
It takes all evening. By the end {sac_he} is laughing at the younger one's terrible hat.

events.text: {sac_name} has started giving things away: a good sword to a junior, a manual to a library, a jade pin to you. "I will not need it," {sac_he} says, lightly, as if talking about the weather. You know exactly what kind of weather {sac_he} means.

effects.log: "Keep it until you need it," you say. {sac_name} looks at you strangely, and takes it back.
You keep the pin. You know you will give something much bigger back, if it comes to that.

events.text: You spend a season at {sac_name}'s side: mornings at the wall of {sac_his} meditation, evenings at the table. Nothing changes. Everything feels a little lighter.

effects.log: You talk about the day you met. {sac_name} remembers it differently, and you argue about it happily for an hour.
Your two breaths fall into step. For a moment you can almost feel the wall yourself, a hand's width in front of {sac_his} heart.

events.text: {sac_name} stands in the courtyard at {sac_realm}, steady, whole, the wall behind {sac_him} at last. Then {sac_he} turns and sees you on the steps, emptied, a realm lower than this morning, and understands what you did, and walks across the courtyard and does not say anything for a long time.

effects.log: "I know," says {sac_name}. "That is what I cannot bear." {sac_He} does not let go of your hands.
"You owe me a realm," you say. {sac_name} laughs and weeps at the same time, which you did not know a person could do.

events.text: Two realms. You poured two realms of your own life into {sac_name}, and {sac_he} went through the wall and the one after it like a stone through paper, and now stands at {sac_realm}, shining with it. You are sitting on the floor. You have never felt so light, or so tired.

effects.log: {sac_name} lifts you as if you weigh nothing. To {sac_him}, now, you do.

choices.text: Tell {sac_him} to go and use it

effects.log: "Go and be what you were meant to be," you say. "And tell me about it after."

events.text: The wall gives. Not because of anything you gave, or anything anyone did: one morning it simply gives, the way a river lets go of a stone. {sac_name} comes out of seclusion at {sac_realm}, blinking, and finds you waiting at the door, which is the first thing {sac_he} wanted to see.

effects.log: You hold on until {sac_name} complains. You do not care.
You burn half of it. {sac_name} eats all of it, and calls it the best meal of {sac_his} life.

events.text: {sac_name} met the wall alone, as {sac_he} always said {sac_he} would, and broke it. When you visit, {sac_he} is sitting in the sun at {sac_realm}, looking younger. "You were ready to give me something," {sac_he} says. "I saw it in your face. Thank you for not having to."

effects.log: "I know," says {sac_name}. "That is how I got through."
You sit until the sun goes down. Nothing needs to be said.

events.text: {sac_name} went into seclusion to meet the wall alone, and did not wake. They find {sac_him} sitting upright, peaceful, hands still in the last seal. On the table by the door, weighted with the jade pin, is a letter with your name on it. It says only: "Not your fault. Not anyone's. Live long."

choices.text: Keep the letter and the pin

effects.log: You keep them both. The pin goes in your hair, or your sleeve, every day after.
You sit in the same room for seven days. On the seventh, something like peace comes, and you leave.

events.text: A bandit chief on the east road boasts that he will rob you. The next morning he is found tied to his own gate with a polite note: "This person is under my protection. {sac_name}, of {sac_realm}." You did not ask for it. {sac_name} will not discuss it.

effects.log: The bandit is very grateful, and very quiet, and moves to another province.
"It is nothing," says {sac_name}. "It is the very least of what I owe you."

events.text: {sac_name} comes every winter now and sits with you in your meditation, pouring a little of {sac_his} own qi back into your meridians, a drop at a time. "I cannot give it all back," {sac_he} says. "But I can give it back slowly, for the rest of my life."

effects.log: The winters are warmer. Your energy rises a little faster every year.
"I gave it to you to keep," you say. {sac_name} ignores you, as usual.

events.text: At a great gathering of the murim, someone asks {sac_name}, now a master of {sac_realm}, how {sac_he} broke through the wall that everyone said would hold. {sac_name} looks across the hall straight at you, and tells them the truth.

effects.log: The hall turns to look at you. Some of them bow.
Too late. Everyone knows now. People treat you differently, and some of them treat you better.

events.text: On a mountain you have never climbed there is a small shrine with a lamp that is always lit. The keeper says a great master named {sac_past} built it long ago, for a friend who gave their life so the master could break through, and made the keepers promise never to let the lamp go out.

effects.log: You trim the wick. The flame stands up straight, as if it knows your hands.

choices.text: Ask what the friend was like

effects.log: "Stubborn," says the keeper. "That is all the master ever said. Stubborn, and kind." You laugh without knowing why.

events.text: Meditating, you find a strange place in your own meridians: a hollow, as if something were poured out of them once, long ago, and the soul still remembers the shape. A name rises with it, {sac_past}, and a feeling of a debt that was paid in full, by someone else, in winters.

effects.log: The hollow fills a little, warm as a winter visit. Your breath comes easier.
You say it into the quiet room. Nothing answers. Something is glad.
